pages.label: Introduction
pages.summary: What Gasket is, how work moves through it, who does what and what you need to run your own copy.

pages.label: Getting started
pages.summary: Start Gasket on your computer with one line, finish setup, set up your site and register your first equipment.

pages.label: Preventive work
pages.summary: Write checklists, schedule them by calendar or meter, create due work orders and assign them.

pages.label: Doing the work
pages.summary: Record checklist results, photos, readings, parts, downtime and findings, then submit the work for review.

pages.label: Review and the board
pages.summary: Approve or return finished work, watch overdue work and downtime, and read every asset's history.

pages.label: Parts and assets
pages.summary: Keep the parts list and physical counts, the asset register, meters and sightings.

pages.label: People, access and agents
pages.summary: Give and end access, choose roles, and let an agent prepare proposals a person approves.

pages.label: Move in from MaintainX
pages.summary: Export from MaintainX, read the dry run, apply it and undo it if needed.

pages.label: Backup and restore
pages.summary: Save your Gasket to one archive with rer export and restore it into a fresh installation with rer import.

pages.label: MaintainX mapping
pages.summary: How each MaintainX export column maps into Gasket, and what is not carried.

pages.label: API for agents
pages.summary: The JSON API Gasket's screens and agents share: signing in, reading, actions and proposals.
